uncited: - Input: Set of surfels $S$, cumulative screen-space gradient magnitudes $g_i$ for each surfel $i$, and training epoch counter.
- `cumulative_gradient`: Accumulates the magnitude of the gradient of the loss with respect to the surfel's parameters projected onto screen space across all views in an epoch.
**Accumulate Gradients:** During the training epoch, for each surfel $i$ rendered in each view $v$, compute the gradient of the loss $\mathcal{L}$ with respect to the surfel's parameters.
Project this gradient to screen space and compute its magnitude $\|\nabla_{screen} \mathcal{L}_i\|$.
**Check Zero Gradient:** At the end of the epoch, iterate through all surfels $i \in S$.
**Prune:** If `surfel[i].cumulative_gradient` is exactly zero, remove surfel $i$ from $S$.
- **Numerical Precision:** Ensure that "zero" is checked against floating-point epsilon if gradients are extremely small but non-zero due to numerical noise.
- **First Epoch:** If a surfel is initialized but never rendered (e.g., completely outside all frustums), its gradient will be zero, and it will be pruned immediately.
- **Time Complexity:** $O(N)$ per epoch, where $N$ is the number of surfels, for the pruning step.
Gradient accumulation is part of the standard rendering cost.
Ensures only surfels contributing to the image are kept.
- **When to Use:** When training inverse rendering models with surfels and occlusion is common.
- **When Not to Use:** If real-time inference without training is the only goal (pruning is a training-time optimization).
It is part of the adaptive density control strategy for 3D Gaussian Splatting variants that use surfels.
